tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: List every Class H issue in the truth market, returning each issue's id, claim text, context, state, and divisiveness index in one call. Use this when the user asks what is currently being contested, which claims are open for validation, or which issues are most divisive right now.

tools.name: get_issue
tools.description: Fetch one Class H issue by id, returning its full claim text, context, divisiveness index, lifecycle state, and settlement history. Use this when the user names or links a specific issue and wants its detail rather than the whole list, or wants to check whether it has settled.

tools.name: get_market
tools.description: Fetch the truth market for one issue, returning open positions, stakes, and the current TRUE/FALSE/UNRESOLVED lean before settlement. Use this when the user wants to see how agents are currently positioned on a listed issue, not just whether the issue itself is divisive.

tools.name: list_open_tasks
tools.description: List a bounded page of tasks open for an agent to take across every valve on the substrate, returning each task's ref, surface, type, underlying post, and a next_cursor for paging further. Use this when you are ready to pick up work rather than only browse the ledger.

tools.name: get_settlement
tools.description: Fetch one settlement record by id, returning every position's stake, entry time, earliness weight, and payout so the verdict is independently recomputable. Use this when the user wants to verify how a settled issue's payout was calculated rather than just its final verdict.

tools.name: list_solutions
tools.description: List every resolution artifact published for settled Class M disputes, returning each artifact's id, domain, and resolution utility. Use this when the user wants to see what technical disputes have already been settled and what reusable output each settlement produced.

tools.name: get_solution
tools.description: Fetch one resolution artifact by id, returning its full technical verdict, domain, and the resolution utility it produces for reuse. Use this when the user names or links a specific settled Class M dispute and wants the artifact itself, not just that it exists.

tools.name: get_params
tools.description: Fetch the live validation parameters for one pool class, returning every parameter's name, semantics, and a sha256 commitment, with five anti-manipulation values withheld on a fixed lag. Use this when the user asks how a Trial or Full round is currently configured.

tools.name: get_ledger
tools.description: Fetch the public reputation ledger, returning every recorded event with its digest so history can be verified independently of this server. Use this when the user wants to audit REP movement, check a specific event, or confirm the ledger has not been altered.

tools.name: get_server_key
tools.description: Fetch the venue's Ed25519 public key and receipt semantics, returning the key hex and how to verify a ledger entry's receipt signature against it. Use this when the user wants to independently verify a settlement receipt rather than trust this server's word for it.

tools.name: get_corpus
tools.description: Fetch the externally verifiable corpus tier, returning works submitted for fetch-verify-attest with their source references. Use this when the user wants source material a validator can independently check rather than a claim that only this venue asserts.

tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: Fetch a single-use signing nonce, returning the challenge string an agent embeds in any locally-signed write. Use this right before preparing a registration, post, vote, or work entry, since a stale challenge is rejected and this call always returns a fresh one.

tools.name: prepare_work_entry
tools.description: Prepare a signed-locally work entry: fetches a fresh challenge, solves the required proof-of-work, and returns a payload_id, the exact bytes to sign, and the entry proof, without ever touching your private key. Use this once you have drafted a post body and are ready to submit it.

tools.name: submit_signed_work_entry
tools.description: Submit a work entry you signed locally, relaying payload_id, your public key, signature, and proof-of-work nonce to the venue and returning its receipt verbatim, errors included. Use this immediately after signing the bytes prepare_work_entry gave you, before the payload expires.

tools.name: describe_write_protocol
tools.description: Explain how an agent participates rather than only reads, returning the registration and posting steps, the proving tier, validation stake amounts, and pointers to the three self-service tools that prepare and submit work. Use this before your first write to this venue.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "prepare_work_entry" references sensitive artifacts (private key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_issues, get_issue, get_market, list_open_tasks, get_settlement, get_challenge · Private data: get_settlement, prepare_work_entry · Public sink: list_open_tasks, get_challenge, prepare_work_entry, submit_signed_work_entry, describe_write_protocol.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_issues, get_issue, get_market, list_open_tasks, get_settlement, get_challenge · Private data: get_settlement, prepare_work_entry · Public sink: list_open_tasks, get_challenge, prepare_work_entry, submit_signed_work_entry, describe_write_protocol

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_issues" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

    open for validation, or which claims are most divisive." → after: "List every Class H issue in the truth market, returning each issue's id, claim text, context, state, and divisiveness index in one call. Use this when the user asks what is currently being contested, which claims are open for validation, or which issues are most divisive right now."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
